title: Fleet Harmony: Control Suite for Dedicated Capacity Scaling and Throughput Reconciliation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a cohesive Fleet Controls / Control Suite experience in Console that bundles scaling controls, an actionable throughput reconciliation dashboard, and immutable change history for Dedicated capacity pools. This work ties autoscaling policy configuration, committed throughput guarantees, and operator-initiated overrides into a single operator workbench. Goal: reduce operator errors, accelerate incident resolution, and provide a clear audit trail for customer-facing and internal investigations.
acceptance_criteria: Users can create/modify autoscaling policies for a Dedicated pool with validation and inline cost/latency impact estimates
A throughput reconciliation dashboard shows target vs observed throughput, queue latency percentiles, and prediction-backed suggested scale actions for the last 14 days
Any change to scaling config (manual or autoscale) is recorded in the Change History with who/when/why and a diff view
Operators can stage a change (canary) to a subset of nodes and roll it forward or rollback from the UI
APIs are available for programmatic retrieval of change history and for triggering staged rollouts
Telemetry events emitted for each operator action so SRE and billing can reconcile consumption against committed throughput
tasks: Finalize UX flows with Design for control panel, confirmation modals, and diff timeline
Define API contract between Console frontend and autoscaler service (ENG ownership)
Backend: Add change-history event stream + retention policy (30/90/365 days)
Instrumentation: add telemetry events for throughput target changes, override events, and reconcile runs
Dashboard: implement reconciliation queries and aggregation for 1m/5m/60m windows
QA: chaos test autoscaler behavior during network partitions and validate rollback UX
Create rollout plan and feature flag gating for 5 pilot customers
notes: Motivated by recent customer support alerts where committed throughput didn't match observed egress due to a misconfigured autoscale rule
We want a single surface that prevents common mistakes like setting scale min > max or confusing 'burst' budget with 'reserved' capacity
Design asked for a compact diff timeline instead of a full audit table to make operator decision loops quicker
Cost impact estimate should be shown as a rough token/hour delta based on recent traffic distribution
